To locate the stationary points of y=f(x), first differentiate f(x) to get f '(x). Then set this derivative equal to zero and solve for x. Each solution corresponds to a potential stationary point. Next, substitute these x-values into f(x) to find their corresponding y-values. Finally, examine the second derivative or use other tests to classify each point as a maximum, minimum, or saddle point.
